Question B-003-020-002.

Why the correct answer is right: A transmission-line surge protector should be outside near the grounding electrode system so surge energy is diverted before the cable enters the shack.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Close to the antenna": A protector at the antenna can still leave a long conductor carrying surge energy toward the building entry without a short bond to the grounding system.
- sourceIndex 2: "Behind the transceiver": Placing the protector behind the radio lets the surge travel through the room and equipment area before it is diverted.
- sourceIndex 3: "Anywhere on the line": Location and bonding length matter. A protector is not equally effective at any random point on the feed line.
